# Review report: fable_5_1-sched (section 3.B items 1-6)

Scope reviewed: `git diff fable_5_1...fable_5_1-sched` (32 files). No finding touches walk results, persisted counters (`containment_checks` / `containment_maintenance_checks`), retire sets, index layout, ledger transfers, replay tokens, checkpoint format, min-ID semantics, coordinator panic paths or Pool locking. Everything below is telemetry, efficiency, cap consistency, documentation or test coverage. Duplicate findings (three on duty-bucket overlap, two on the service-step Delegate stall, two on the shards cap) are merged.

## Contested finding

| Location | Claim | Verifier A (confirmed, minor) | Verifier B (refuted) |
|----------|-------|-------------------------------|----------------------|
| `W/execution.rs:1195-1201` (`ready_escrow_limits`: `bytes = 2 * CHUNK_BYTES * inspectors`) | The byte cap is reached before the `2 x inspectors` entry cap because `Escrow::charge` adds spare `Vec` capacity and entry overhead on top of a payload that can equal `CHUNK_BYTES`; `reclaim_all_finished` then silently `continue`s and the slot stays occupied; no counter records the skip; Ready tests never fill the store. | Mechanism holds: a byte-full tail chunk charges strictly more than `CHUNK_BYTES` (spare <= payload since the Vec grows from `Vec::new()` via `mem::take`, parallel.rs:586), so 2n full entries never fit in 2n x CHUNK_BYTES; n to 2n-1 fit depending on spare. The skip is silent (no counter). Requires many near-full tail chunks on short jobs during one commit; edge case, Ready-only, lost recycling opportunity only, no correctness effect. `parallel/tests/escrow.rs:176-217` does exercise the byte cap for `reclaim_finished`, not for `reclaim_all_finished`. Fix: size bytes from the real worst-case charge (or drop the byte cap for Ready), add a `completed_escrow_reclaim_skipped` counter, test filling the store. | Contract is a ceiling ("at most two completed results per inspector"), not a guarantee that 2I fit; `Escrow::charge` is byte-identical to fable_5_1 and Ordered has always applied it. Worst-case full-chunk charge is ~9.6 MiB (spare <= 16,384 x size_of::<Event>) so 16 MiB x I admits >= ~1.67 I entries, not ~I. Scenario needs > I unpolled near-full residual chunks in one commit, which publish blocking (parallel.rs:308-313) and no-polling-inside-commit make implausible. Existing snapshot keys (`completed_escrow_accounted_bytes` vs `_max_`, `completed_escrow_reserve_fallback`, `finished_awaiting_poll`, `ready_service_reclaimed_slots`) already make a skip observable. Coverage nit at most. |

Reporter note: both verifiers agree the byte ceiling is undershot relative to the arithmetic intent of `2 * CHUNK_BYTES * inspectors` and that `reclaim_all_finished` lacks a byte-cap test; they disagree only on whether this is worth a code change. A one-line comment stating the effective bound plus the missing test resolves both positions.

## Refuted

- "Ready escrow cap adds up to 2W parked chunks on top of the W slot-held chunks the old Ready path bounded" (`W/execution.rs:1195`) — refuted by both verifiers.

## Merge recommendation

**Merge after fixes.** The six in-scope items hold their invariants: identical results and persisted counters for the bit pre-filter and prepared retirement, unchanged Ordered behaviour, exact Ready obligation accounting, checkpoint format unchanged, replay tokens untouched, no new coordinator panic or Pool blocking paths. Every finding is in new additive telemetry, coordinator efficiency, cap consistency, docs or tests.

Minimal fix list before merging into fable_5_1:

1. Emit `coordinator_duty` at `progress.parallel.coordinator_duty` in `enrich_with` (or fix `heartbeat_metrics.py:65` at merge) and cross-check with a Rust test (finding 1).
2. Make the merge gate pass: nest `containment_prefilter` under `parallel` or add it to `IGNORED_TOP_LEVEL`, and handle `descendant_closure.refresh_duty_bound` for old-vs-new strict compares (finding 7).
3. Stop double-charging `duty.dispatch` under Ready (subtract nested publication/progress/checkpoint) or drop the `buckets_are_disjoint` claim; emit `coordinator_duty` once per event (finding 2).
4. `snapshot_lean()` for the per-domain `set_parallel` at execution.rs:1403 and :1420 (finding 5).
5. Early return in `reclaim_all_finished` when the escrow entry cap is hit or `reserve_failed` (finding 4).
6. Nest the two `ready_service` counts in `duty_json` so the monitor does not read them as duty shares (finding 9).
7. Raise `shards/config.rs:62/:73` to 256 or document the 64 cap (finding 10).
8. Update plan B3 text to the rule pinned by `worker_budget/tests.rs:112-137` (finding 11).

Recommended but not blocking: defer-and-skip unpublished Delegates in the service step with a stall counter and a Delegate-seeding test (finding 3); gate the per-slot arrays to drain/final report (finding 6); reclassify empty prepared sets (finding 8); ungated synchronous `reclaim_all_finished` test (finding 12); frozen lean key-set assertions (finding 13); byte-cap comment and `reclaim_all_finished` byte-cap test (contested item).
